survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD country note summarises system-level indicators from Education at a Glance 2025 rather than estimating student-level model parameters. No student microdata sampling frame, replicate design, or explicit complex-survey weighting variables are described in the note. The figures reported (e.g., attainment shares, completion rates, expenditure per student) are presented as descriptive statistics for the latest available reference year(s) and are not accompanied by an analysis plan that would specify weight variables (e.g., W_FSTUWT) or replicate-weight procedures. For any secondary analysis using the underlying OECD indicator datasets, analysts should follow the indicator-specific methodology and technical notes referenced by the publication, because weighting and coverage can differ by indicator.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This document is a descriptive country note reporting education-system indicators (attainment, employment/earnings gaps, completion, dropout, international student mobility, and expenditure). It does not conduct an ILSA-style student-level achievement analysis that would require plausible values (PV) generation/combination. Missing-data handling is therefore not applicable to the note’s presentation of published indicator results, and the note does not provide an imputation/deletion protocol.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Used the latest available data for Luxembourg as compiled in Education at a Glance 2025; the note does not specify an analytic subsample or student-level inclusion/exclusion criteria.

data.outcome_summary: This OECD Education at a Glance 2025 country note provides a descriptive overview of Luxembourg’s education system, with emphasis on tertiary education. It reports indicator values for the latest available year(s), including attainment outcomes for young adults (25–34), employment and earnings differences by educational attainment, and progression measures such as bachelor’s entry pathways, completion within theoretical and extended timeframes, and first-year dropout rates. It also summarises participation and system characteristics (e.g., age-grade mismatch in lower secondary, international student mobility in tertiary education) and resource indicators (government expenditure per student by education level and funding shares from public vs private sources). The note does not present an assessment instrument, student-level sampling design, plausible values, or a statistical/ML modeling strategy; therefore, no predictive performance metrics or causal effects are estimated. Policy relevance is drawn from the comparative indicator patterns across OECD averages rather than from model-based inference.
data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse because this is not an empirical ML/predictive study using ILSA microdata; it is a descriptive OECD country note. As a result, there is no student-level dataset, no PV-based achievement outcome, no missing-data/imputation strategy, and no ML algorithm evaluation to extract. The absence of main findings rows and confounders is consistent with the document’s purpose: summarising published education indicators rather than conducting an original analytical model.
